propositions: Pass-1 escalation on provider context limit uses MODULE_LADDER bare model ids instead of respecting the run's configured provider qualifier, causing provider mismatch when the run is bedrock-qualified with no model-class table

The decision about escalation target is made from module constants alone without consulting the actual run model, so _rung_target cannot distinguish between a bedrock-qualified primary and an unqualified one
_rung_target compares rung's self-inferred provider against class-resolved provider but never checks the run's primary model's provider
The one-criterion entry rung uses bare anthropic ids from MODEL_LADDER, so even the common retry path crosses providers when the class table is unconfigured
When provider-qualified primary model and unconfigured class table combine, escalation silently substitutes a bare anthropic id that fails in provider-isolated containers or incurs unbudgeted spend
The fix threads the primary model into _rung_target and drops escalation rungs whose inferred provider differs from the primary's when both are determinable
